issue_request: FHIR-17469 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core validation issue reporting that the standard Java JAR validator accepted an Observation with a closed slice on code.coding, one required 1..1 slice, and an additional unsliced coding; the requested behavior was for validation to reject the extra repetition.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-17469 source commit or relevant source mention was found in the current FHIR spec checkout. The closed-slicing code definition and validator capability table predate the issue, so the source semantics appear to have already matched the reporter's interpretation.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread confirms the interpretation: Lloyd McKenzie said the behavior sounded like a validator bug, and Martijn Harthoorn reported the .NET validator rejected the example. The active profiling and validation pages are in the build hierarchy, and this checkout has no Java validator source to patch. No Confluence references for FHIR-17469 were found.
reconciliation: No FHIR spec source files were changed. The reconciliation published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch to record that any remaining fix belongs in the Java validator implementation, not in this specification source checkout.

evidence_items.learned: The authoritative source already conveys that extra unsliced repetitions are invalid for closed slicing.
